issues.description: run() loop lacks termination invariant; train() can overshoot max_step or spin forever on empty iterator
issues.detail: The outer while loop checks global_step < max_step only between epochs. train() runs save_interval batches unconditionally, overshooting by up to save_interval-1 steps. Worse, if the data iterator yields zero batches, global_step never advances and the loop spins forever, re-saving the same checkpoint. State and enforce the invariant inside train().

issues.description: Checkpoint discovery uses fragile split('step_')[-1] parsing that crashes or silently misorders on near-miss names
issues.detail: The filter accepts any directory containing 'step_' anywhere, then splits and takes the last segment as int(). 'step_3_backup' raises ValueError; 'foo_step_10' is silently accepted. The naming invariant is neither stated nor checked. Use a regex full-match on 'step_<int>' and skip non-matches.

issues.description: trainer_args key mismatch: docstring promises max_steps/val_interval, code reads max_step and ignores val_interval
issues.detail: The constructor docstring advertises max_steps, log_interval, val_interval, save_interval; the code reads max_step (singular) and never consults val_interval or log_interval. save_interval secretly drives training chunk size, validation cadence, and checkpoint cadence at once. Reconcile names, document actual cadence, and validate the precondition at construction.

issues.description: _all_reduce_stats silently assumes identical key set and call order across ranks; mismatch hangs or corrupts
issues.detail: The function iterates `for key in stats` and issues a SUM all_reduce per key, dividing by world_size. NCCL requires every rank to call the same collectives in the same order. If a rank skips a metric (empty batch, missing key), the job hangs or produces wrong means. State and assert the precondition, or all_reduce a presence mask.

issues.description: Trainer complects engine, wandb logging, checkpoint discovery, dtype derivation, and reduction into one class with hidden global state
issues.detail: DeepSpeedTrainer braids five separable concerns and depends on a module-level wandb singleton initialized elsewhere. Behavior depends on implicit global state that is asserted by docstring rather than code. Pass a logger object explicitly, extract pure helpers (precision_from_config, checkpoint discovery), and shrink the class to orchestration only.

issues.description: Data specifier strings are stringly-typed and re-parsed in multiple places without a stated grammar
issues.detail: valid_*_specifier uses 'task:name[:factor]' format split on whitespace in train.py with no validation that tokens match the grammar. The same parsing logic recurs downstream. Parse once at the edge into a small dataclass {task, name, path, factor}; a typo would then fail at startup rather than silently mis-keying a validation set.

synthesis.summary: The panel rejects this PR as under-reasoned. Two correctness defects block merge: the run() loop has no termination invariant (overshoots max_step or spins forever on an empty iterator) and checkpoint discovery uses a fragile split that crashes or silently misorders on near-miss directory names. The trainer_args contract is incoherent — docstring and code disagree on the key bounding the training loop, and save_interval secretly drives three different cadences. Distributed collective discipline in _all_reduce_stats is asserted by hope rather than invariant, the classic 3am-hang failure mode. Beyond correctness, the trainer class complects engine, logging, checkpoint, dtype, and reduction concerns through hidden global wandb state.
